data.narrative:
Q-Factor is a seed-stage quantum computing company founded by Nir Davidson, Ofer Firstenberg, Yoav Sagi, and Guy Raz. The company has raised $24M to date. The quantum computing sector includes 3 public companies (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private peers including Quantinuum, IonQ, PsiQuantum, D-Wave Quantum, and SandboxAQ.

Valuation was estimated using stage-progression methodology, the only applicable triangulation approach given data constraints. This method applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage transitions to the $24M total raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $60M. A peer-median approach could not be applied: while 8 same-sector peers exist, none met narrow filtering criteria (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier), and a broad all-sector median would introduce excessive noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $51M to $69M, centered at $60M. This range reflects uncertainty inherent in applying a single methodology to an early-stage company in a capital-intensive, pre-commercialization sector. Key uncertainties include the appropriate step-up multiplier for quantum computing ventures specifically and the lack of comparable seed-stage transactions in the narrow peer set. Investors should treat this as a starting point for diligence rather than a definitive valuation.
